item: native_call.__enter__ undoes its bump when an interrupt lands before it returns
summary: From the independent read of PR 1468: __enter__ caught only Exception, so a KeyboardInterrupt on the main thread between the slot bump and the return left the slot at 1 until restart (__exit__ never runs for an entry that raised) and every later abort read as in flight; the dns and connect brackets in airplane.py share it. It now catches the interrupt, undoes the bump and re-raises. If the interrupt lands before the bump's own write, the undo lowers a concurrent holder's count by one for as long as that call lasts (clamped at zero): a short undercount is the lesser error. __exit__ is not given the same retry (an interrupt inside the decrement itself is a stated limit). Red without the change.
